subject: EdgeForge performance constraints + runbook / next steps
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Tracy Li <tracy.li@edgeforge.ai>, Samir Ahmad <samir@edgeforge.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-14T15:32:00-07:00
Subject: EdgeForge performance constraints + runbook / next steps

Hi Tracy / Samir —

Thanks again for the call today. Below is a short recap of what we heard, the technical constraints you highlighted, and proposed next steps so everyone is aligned. If I missed anything, flag it and I’ll update.

Summary of pain & goals
- Primary goal: move latency-sensitive search/assist features from CPU-based service to LLM inference with under 200ms p95 on single-request interactive flows.
- Target throughput: sustained ~120–150 qps during daytime peak; 300 qps burst for short windows.
- Models: want to validate 70B family (you indicated Llama-2-chat-70b-quant) and a smaller 13B fallback for cost control.
- Data concerns: tenant isolation and audit logs are required (SOC2 scope).

Key constraints we captured
- p95 latency target: 200ms (end-to-end, inclusive of network hop to inference node).
- Token length: typical prompt+response = 80–220 tokens; KV cache reuse expected for follow-ups.
- Deployment preference: Dedicated pool in us-west initially; potential later move to VPC-private for compliance.
- Cost sensitivity: want conservative cost estimate for 150 qps baseline; look for batching profiles that keep tail latency within SLO.

Technical risks we should validate in the deep dive
- Whether a quantized 70B can meet 200ms p95 on your workload when using our autoscaling + batching policies.
- KV cache hit rates and sequence-length variability impacting batching efficiency.
- Network egress and cross-AZ hops adding 20–40ms in your current topology.

Proposed next steps
1) Tech deep-dive (60m) with EdgeForge infra + Redwood runtime engineers — goal: agree on topology and sizing assumptions (Marcus/Ben to lead).
2) Runbook + benchmarking plan: Redwood will draft a short runbook with measurement scripts and expected metrics to run during POC (attached draft).
3) Procurement checklist: we’ll send a simple procurement checklist for Dedicated seat sizing and required security questionnaires.

Availability: Marcus proposed Aug 16 or 17 for the deep-dive — Marcus / Ben / Neha, can you confirm?

Thanks — looking forward to the next call.

—
Hannah Schmitt

Thanks Hannah — great summary. A couple clarifications from our side:
- The 200ms p95 target is for the user-facing inference call only; our current request path adds ~25ms on average after hitting the model, so we were implicitly budgeting ~175ms at the inference layer.
- Burst windows are typically 3–6 minutes during analytics jobs; sustaining 150 qps for 6+ hours is not required.
- We have a compliance kickoff next week; SOC2 evidence will be needed but the initial POC can run with redacted logs.

We’re available Aug 16 09:00–11:00 PT for the deep-dive. I’ll add our infra lead (Samir) to that slot. Please share the runbook draft and any measurement scripts prior to the call.

On Sat, Aug 14, 2027 at 5:05 PM Tracy Li <tracy.li@edgeforge.ai> wrote:
> Thanks Hannah — great summary. A couple clarifications from our side:...

Quick technical notes ahead of the deep-dive:
- For a quantized 70B we should plan for model sharding across 4 x A10x GPUs (or equivalent) to hit low tail latency; with token lengths you described and continuous KV cache reuse we expect average token latency to be low but cold starts will spike.
- Recommended batching profile for initial POC: target batch size 4, max latency budget 120ms for the aggregator before hitting model. That generally preserves p95 if network hop is ~25ms.
- For throughput: 150 qps sustained equates to ~18k tokens/sec if average response is 120 tokens; ensure we validate tokenization variance in the runbook.
- We’ll instrument trace headers (x-rw-trace-id) so you can correlate our logs with your frontend dashboards.

I’ll prepare a quick appendix with expected capacity numbers for 13B vs 70B and drop it into the runbook doc.

—Ben

Thanks all — confirmed for Aug 16 09:30 PT (adjusted 30m to accommodate calendars). Agenda snapshot:
1) Walk through EdgeForge request path and where inference is invoked (Samir).
2) Redwood topology options: Dedicated single AZ vs Dedicated multi-AZ with warm standby (Ben).
3) Profiling plan & measurement script review (Ben/Neha).
4) Risk review: cold start mitigation, cache TTLs, and autoscaling sensitivity (Marcus).

Attachments: I attached a short procurement checklist (edgeforge-procurement-checklist.pdf) and a skeleton runbook (redwood-inference-quick-runbook.md) with test scripts and expected outputs. Please review before the call — we’ll use the doc as the working artifact.

Deliverable expectations by EOD Aug 20:
- Agreement on topology and sizing (Redwood + EdgeForge)
- Initial benchmark results from your side running the measurement script
- A procurement seat estimate we can convert to an initial Dedicated commitment

If anything changes with timing, ping here and we’ll adapt.
